evidence_tree.note: The scenario definition and the golden baseline live outside the permitted export (scripts/, tests/), so the event at index 17 could not be read directly. The identification below is derived from the scenario name plus the cached effect roster.

atoms include 'damage.resistance-mitigation' (behavior: Carve) — Black Cleaver is the resistance-side effect in this scenario.

Bloodsong atoms are damage.basic_attack / damage.bonus / damage.on_hit / damage.physical (all evidence 'passive:Spellblade'), plus stats/vision/economy atoms. There is NO resistance-mitigation / armor-reduction atom anywhere in Bloodsong's decomposition.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> other Bounty-of-Worlds upgrades in the support roster
sources_quoted.text: 3869 Celestial Opposition = incoming damage reduction + slow (untyped); 3870 Dream Maker = damage reduction bubble + 'bonus magic damage'; 3871 Zaz'Zak's Realmspike = 'magic damage' explosion; 3876 Solstice Sleigh = bonus movement speed + bonus health. None of the four produces an armor-mitigated effect.
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R); reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R <- R - r_flat; R <- R*(1 - r_pct/100). Resistance-side effects act on R; they are not damage amplifiers.
'below {{rd|50%|30%}} of its maximum health' and 'granting you {{g|{{rd|22|20}}}}' — the template is {{rd|melee|ranged}}, so Expose Weakness is 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder).

independent_computation.step_1_what_the_field_means: resistance_type names the resistance that mitigates the event: 'armor' for physical damage, 'magic' for magic damage, absent for anything that is not mitigated by a resistance (true damage, heals/shields, and pure effect applications such as amplifiers).
independent_computation.step_2_enumerate_armor_typed_effects_ava: Across the whole support-item roster (World Atlas -> Runic Compass -> Bounty of Worlds -> {Bloodsong, Celestial Opposition, Dream Maker, Solstice Sleigh, Zaz'Zak's Realmspike}) the ONLY armor-mitigated damage instance is Bloodsong's Spellblade proc (100% base AD bonus PHYSICAL damage on-hit). Every other support-side effect is magic damage (Zaz'Zak, Dream Maker purple bubble), a heal/bonus-health/movement grant (Solstice Sleigh), a damage reduction (Celestial Opposition, Dream Maker blue bubble), vision (Ward), or gold.
independent_computation.step_3_classify_expose_weakness: Expose Weakness is quoted verbatim as 'causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources'. 'From all sources' means it multiplies physical, magic AND true damage alike; it is a post-mitigation damage amplifier, not a resistance modifier and not itself a damage instance. Therefore an Expose Weakness event is type-agnostic and must carry NO resistance_type. Confirmed structurally by the atom decomposition: Bloodsong has zero resistance-mitigation atoms, while Black Cleaver (the other named item in the scenario) owns the sole damage.resistance-mitigation atom.
independent_computation.step_4_index_binding: support_events is the ally/support-side ledger of the coupled participant timeline. Under any ordering that groups by item, Bloodsong (id 3877, the highest id in the roster and the item the scenario is named for) contributes exactly two event kinds at the tail of the ledger: (a) the Spellblade physical damage instance -> resistance_type 'armor', and (b) the Expose Weakness application -> no resistance_type. A single trailing leaf losing 'armor' while the roster's other leaves keep their typing is the signature of (b) shedding an incorrect armor tag, not of (a) losing its mitigation type (which would have to move the mitigated-damage numbers on the same event, and would contradict the four physical-damage atoms Bloodsong does have).

step_5_why_the_wrong_tag_matters_numeric.setup: raw = 100 physical, defender armor = 100, Black Cleaver at 5 Carve stacks (30% armor reduction), melee Bloodsong holder (Expose Weakness = 8%).
step_5_why_the_wrong_tag_matters_numeric.error: 4.25% understatement on physical damage, and the amplifier is lost entirely on magic and true damage (100 true damage should read 108, not 100). This is exactly the mis-composition a scenario coupling Black Cleaver with Bloodsong is built to catch.
step_5_why_the_wrong_tag_matters_numeric.conclusion: Tagging the Expose Weakness event 'armor' would put a global amplifier into the armor pipeline alongside Carve. Dropping the tag is the correct, fail-closed representation.

independent_computation.step_6_verdict: The removal is correct: no Bloodsong-sourced effect other than the Spellblade damage instance is armor-mitigated, and Expose Weakness ('increased damage from all sources') is by definition untyped.

caveat: The scenario definition and golden baseline are outside the permitted evidence tree, so support_events[17] could not be inspected. The verdict holds on the stated identification (index 17 = the Bloodsong Expose Weakness / non-damage effect event). If index 17 is instead the Spellblade physical damage instance itself, the correct value would be 'armor' and the verdict would flip to old_value_correct — the deciding test is whether the event at that index carries a mitigated damage amount. Everything in the permitted evidence points to a non-damage amplifier event.
